tier_reason: c_latest.json.gz (run 2026-09-29-182101) carries every quoted iqr_1.5 mean (libbson 157,288 / 546,018 / 962,634 / 1,168,630 / 324,854 ns vs cJSON 338,949 / 855,914 / 3,078,222 / 669,472 / 502,002 ns at 100 instances) plus gcc 11.4.0 and the i7-12800H; the harness code (c/src/serializers/ser_libbson.c, ser_cjson.c, c/CMakeLists.txt -O2, c/scripts/fetch-and-build-deps.sh) is public, so A holds as reproducible evidence even though the comparison itself is weak and cross-format.

corrections.caveats: Weak, indirect evidence. Nobody claims libbson is faster than a named baseline; the only comparison is a third-party multi-format shootout in which libbson beats the C JSON libraries on four of five payloads but loses to yyjson, mpack and libcbor, and loses to cJSON, json-c and parson on the strings payload. The comparison is cross-format (BSON vs JSON text) and off the category's baselines: in the same run libbson is slower than every MessagePack, Protobuf and FlatBuffers row (msgpack-c, mpack, Google protobuf and flatcc, plus the protobuf-c and nanopb rows, which time a shared in-tree wire codec) on all five payloads at both 100 and 1 instance, for example document at 100 instances 546,018 ns vs msgpack-c 208,797, Google protobuf 226,492 and flatcc 75,146 (derived from page data); among binary rows only ion-c is slower, and only on message, document and event. It says nothing about libbson against any other BSON implementation. The harness reader (c/src/serializers/ser_libbson.c) is pessimized for libbson: enter_elem finds each array element by its decimal key with bson_iter_init_find (a linear scan from the array start, so quadratic in array length) and copies every scalar array element into a freshly bson_init'ed wrapper document that is then destroyed; this probably explains the strings loss (decode 909,025 ns vs cJSON 452,216) and understates libbson. The writer appends every integer as INT64. Builds differ: libbson comes from mongo-c-driver's own CMake Release build (bson_static, -Wno-error), while cJSON is compiled inside the harness, where add_compile_options(-O2) follows CMake's Release flags. The listed repository mongodb/libbson is archived (2020-10-13) with last commit 2017-12-20 (version 1.9.0); the benchmark used libbson from mongo-c-driver 1.27.5, so the measured code is not in the listed repository (use https://github.com/mongodb/mongo-c-driver, src/libbson, for the live code). Host used the powersave governor; the run's git tree (commit 7cf1c19) was dirty, most likely with the Ion serializers committed next as f040bcc (ion-c appears in the run's serializer list and f040bcc is the only later change under c/src/serializers), so the libbson and cJSON wrappers at HEAD are what ran. The mongodb/mongo-c-driver-performance suite measures libbson alone with no baseline column (see data/seeds/no_evidence/w6-mine-a.json). The dashboard on github.io is blocked here and was not opened.
corrections.compiler_and_flags: gcc (Ubuntu 11.4.0-1ubuntu1~22.04.3) 11.4.0; harness c/CMakeLists.txt defaults to Release and adds add_compile_options(-O2 -Wall -Wno-unused-function), so in-tree cJSON compiles at -O2; libbson taken from mongo-c-driver 1.27.5, built by c/scripts/fetch-and-build-deps.sh with CMake -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DCMAKE_C_FLAGS=-Wno-error, target bson_static; cJSON v1.7.19, jansson v2.15.1 (CMake Release), json-c 0.15 from the system package (per c/third_party/VERSIONS.md and the run's serializer list).

notes: All quoted numbers and ratios check out against the result file (cJSON figures differ by 1 ns from rounding). Shortcomings to record: cross-format and off-category comparison (slower than every msgpack-c, mpack, protobuf and flatcc row on all ten cells), harness reader pessimizes libbson arrays (quadratic element lookup, per-scalar wrapper docs), loses to cJSON/json-c/parson on strings and to yyjson on 4 of 5, listed repo archived since 2020 with the measured code in mongo-c-driver; consider a repo_url override to https://github.com/mongodb/mongo-c-driver (Apache-2.0, 883 stars). Metadata confirmed (Apache-2.0, 347 stars, archived, last commit 2017-12-20).

tier_reason: c_latest.json.gz has every quoted libcbor, libcbor-stream and tinycbor mean (round trip, encode, decode, 100 and 1 instance) plus gcc 11.4.0 and the i7-12800H; the harness (c/src/serializers/ser_libcbor.c, ser_libcbor_stream.c, ser_libcbor_common.c, ser_tinycbor.c, c/CMakeLists.txt, c/scripts/fetch-and-build-deps.sh) and all build flags are public, so A holds; the access-pattern and flag asymmetries are caveats, not missing methodology.

corrections.caveats: Not a project claim and not a pure parser throughput test: the harness wrappers decide the access pattern. The libcbor rows install a 16 MiB bump-arena allocator through cbor_set_allocs (reset every op, free is a no-op), which the wrapper calls the documented amortization pattern; default malloc-backed libcbor would be slower. The libcbor wrappers were reworked on 2026-08-25 (GLD commit 797bcbb, 'Rework libcbor rows: streaming wrapper, DOM tuning, native decoder') in answer to the call-path review request PJK/libcbor#433, while the tinycbor wrapper got no equivalent tuning: it locates every key with cbor_value_map_find_value (linear scan) and reaches array element i by advancing i times from the start, so its decode time grows quadratically with array length; most of the 4x to 5x decode gaps on strings and telemetry come from that access pattern, not from raw parsing speed. Build flags are asymmetric in libcbor's favour: libcbor v0.11.0 is built by its own CMake Release configuration (-O3 -Wall -DNDEBUG, plus interprocedural optimization when check_ipo_supported passes), while tinycbor is compiled with plain cc -O2 and no -DNDEBUG, so its cbor_assert checks stay live; part of the 1.2x to 1.6x encode-only gap may come from this. The fairest numbers are still the encode-only ones and the single-instance rows. The plain DOM row is slower than tinycbor at serialization and on the event payload. Against the category's MessagePack baseline libcbor is slower in the same run: mpack and msgpack-c beat libcbor-stream on all five payloads at 100 instances (for example telemetry 113,338 and 122,695 ns vs 174,795 ns), and every protobuf-wire and flatcc row is faster still (derived from page data). Results were measured on libcbor v0.11.0, before master's PR #434 (merged 2026-08-23: inline cbor_incref and cbor_decref, said by its author to give about 1.3x to 1.5x on DOM-building workloads). The benchmark's maintainer filed libcbor issues #433 (call-path review request, now closed) and #440/#441 (spec compliance misses, closed), so the suite's own compliance matrix lists libcbor misses. The result file is a dashboard snapshot (dashboard/public/data/c_latest.json.gz, run 2026-09-29-182101, re-folded on 2026-10-05); the interactive dashboard on github.io is blocked here and was not opened. Host used the powersave governor; the run's git tree (commit 7cf1c19) was dirty, most likely with the Ion serializers committed next as f040bcc, the only later change under c/src/serializers, so the libcbor and tinycbor wrappers at HEAD are what ran. About 84 to 96 kept samples per row after IQR filtering. libcbor's own README and docs have no benchmark.
corrections.compiler_and_flags: gcc (Ubuntu 11.4.0-1ubuntu1~22.04.3) 11.4.0; harness c/CMakeLists.txt defaults to Release with add_compile_options(-O2 -Wall -Wno-unused-function); libcbor v0.11.0 built by c/scripts/fetch-and-build-deps.sh with its own CMake Release configuration (libcbor's CMakeLists.txt sets -O3 -Wall -DNDEBUG and enables interprocedural optimization when check_ipo_supported passes), static library; tinycbor v0.6.0 compiled with cc -O2 and no -DNDEBUG (so cbor_assert stays live), symbols prefixed tc_ via objcopy.

notes: Every number in claimed_speedup matches the result file (1 ns rounding differences only). Corrected caveats: #433 is closed, not open; libcbor wrappers were tuned after the #433 review while tinycbor's quadratic access pattern was not; libcbor built -O3 -DNDEBUG (+IPO) vs tinycbor -O2 with asserts; both libcbor rows lose to the category's MessagePack rows (mpack, msgpack-c). Metadata confirmed (MIT, 405 stars, last commit 2026-10-04, active).

tier_reason: LEDGER.md run 3 (2026-09-13, Apple M1 Max, -O3 -DNDEBUG -flto=thin) lists every quoted toml++ and toml11 time, and the code is public (benchmarks/bench_tomlplus.cpp, bench_toml11.cpp, bench_main.cpp, scripts/run_benchmarks.sh: warmup 1, min of 10), but the compiler is never named, so not A; it is an independent third-party measurement by a competing parser's author, so B.

corrections.caveats: The win is against toml11 only. In the same matrix cpptoml (v0.5-era, TOML 0.5 semantics, rejects heterogeneous arrays) parses faster than toml++ on all 8 shapes it can parse (for example cargo_like 4.0 ms vs 7.3 ms, scalar_float 24.3 ms vs 65.2 ms), tomlc17 is faster on array_heavy, deep_tables and mixed (6.8, 2.9 and 4.2 ms vs 12.0, 5.4 and 10.1 ms), tomlc99 is faster on deep_tables (2.9 ms), and teptris (the benchmark author's own C library) is 3.2-7.5x faster than toml++. The benchmark was written by the author of a competing TOML parser (teptris) and published in its own repository, so it is independent of toml++ and toml11 but not a neutral suite; it falls short of tier A because the compiler is not named (Darwin arm64 with -flto=thin implies Apple clang) and the toml++ and toml11 numbers come from a single machine. benchmarks/CMakeLists.txt adds target_compile_options(bench_parse PRIVATE -O2) after the Release -O3, so the header-only toml++ and toml11 adapters most likely compile at -O2 (equal for both). The toml++ row times toml::parse on a string_view; the toml11 row also times a copy into a std::vector (ledger says under 2% of parse). toml11 is pinned at v4.2.0 and its v4.4.0 release notes (2025-02-15) claim toml::parse is 2x faster, so the ratio is overstated against current toml11; toml11 per-token error-location metadata makes it a slow baseline (0.1-1.9 MB/s here), and the toml11 PR #320 author notes that toml11 parses and preserves comments while toml++ does not, so part of the gap is a feature difference. Run on generated corpora (seed 42), not real-world configs. toml++'s own repo has only examples/parse_benchmark.cpp (a timing loop, no comparison) and no published numbers; the PR #320 numbers (10,000 toml::try_parse calls, i5-12600KF) come from an open third-party PR with no compiler or flags stated. Linux x86_64 gcc CI numbers exist in the same ledger but give no toml++ figures.
corrections.compiler_and_flags: Release build per LEDGER.md: -O3 -DNDEBUG -flto=thin (top-level CMakeLists.txt turns on CMAKE_INTERPROCEDURAL_OPTIMIZATION for Release); benchmarks/CMakeLists.txt also adds target_compile_options(bench_parse PRIVATE -O2), so the header-only toml++ v3.4.0 and toml11 v4.2.0 adapters (bench_tomlplus.cpp, bench_toml11.cpp) most likely compile at -O2, equally for both; compiler binary not named (Darwin arm64 with thin LTO implies Apple clang).

notes: All nine toml++ vs toml11 times and the 18x-430x range (17.8x-431x derived) match LEDGER.md; PR #320 figures (1,178.6/1,015.5 vs 17,850.4/18,118.0 and 4,482.6/4,859.9 ms) match the open PR. Shortcomings: win only over toml11 (a slow, comment-preserving baseline pinned before its 2x v4.4.0 speedup); cpptoml faster on all 8 parsable shapes and tomlc17 on 3; benchmark by a competitor; compiler unnamed. Metadata confirmed (MIT, 2.2k stars, last commit 2026-07-21, active). Not a duplicate: teptris is listed separately with toml++ as its baseline.
